originalTitle: Blackbox review – a legendary escape from slavery is told with magic tricks
summary: The story of Henry ‘Box’ Brown, who succeeded in mailing himself out of bondage, is recounted rather than fully dramatised
content: Henry “Box” Brown is wrapped up in chains when he has an idea to claim his freedom. As inspiration hits him, actor Josiah Alpher flexes his muscles and, miraculously, the chains appear to pass through his neck. Magic! It is a neat visual metaphor for a true story that seems miraculous in itself. In 1849, Brown made a break to flee slavery near Richmond, Virginia, by posting himself in a wooden crate to Philadelphia, a state where ownership of human beings had been phased out by the Gradual Abolition Act of 1780. Alpher describes a painful journey, squashed, upturned and knocked about, before Brown’s happy delivery. Rickerby Hinds’s staging of his own play uses the language of stage magic, from the glamorous magician’s assistant (Jada Evelyn Ramsey) to the knotted rope trick, to emphasise how extraordinary this escape was. Brown gets into the box as if he were Harry Houdini performing a stunt. Hinds shows too how the bonds of US slavery were not just represented by physical chains: they extended to a church that sanctioned the practice and to the constant threat of whipping, a nagging psychological burden. All this is duly itemised in a script that tells Brown’s story before his break for freedom, not only the callous treatment at the hands of his owner, but also accounts of conditions even worse than his own. It is weighty material but it is lessened in three ways. The story is recounted rather than dramatised and were it not for the magic tricks would seem theatrically flat. The actors hit an impressively breakneck speed, but perform without tonal variation, making it hard to keep up. And the story ends where you might expect it to begin, with Henry “Box” Brown’s entry into a new life. • At Underbelly, Edinburgh, until 30 August • All our Edinburgh festival reviews
chineseTitle: 黑盒评论——用魔术讲述摆脱奴隶制的传奇故事
chineseSummary: 亨利·“盒子”·布朗成功摆脱束缚的故事是重述的，而不是完全戏剧化的
chineseContent: 当亨利·“博克斯”·布朗想要获得自由时，他却被锁链包裹着。当灵感袭来时，演员乔赛亚·阿尔弗 (Josiah Alpher) 活动了他的肌肉，奇迹般地，链条似乎穿过了他的脖子。魔法！这是对一个本身看起来很神奇的真实故事的简洁视觉隐喻。 1849 年，布朗为了逃离弗吉尼亚州里士满附近的奴隶制，将自己装在一个木箱里，送往费城，该州的人类所有权已因 1780 年的《逐步废奴法案》而被逐步废除。阿尔弗描述了布朗幸福分娩之前的一段痛苦旅程，被压扁、翻倒和撞倒。里克比·海因兹 (Rickerby Hinds) 在自己的戏剧表演中使用了舞台魔术的语言，从迷人的魔术师助手（贾达·伊芙琳·拉姆齐 (Jada Evelyn Ramsey) 饰）到打结的绳子戏法，都强调了这次逃脱是多么的非凡。布朗进入禁区，就像哈利·胡迪尼在表演特技一样。海因兹还展示了美国奴隶制的束缚不仅仅体现在有形的锁链上：它们延伸到了认可这种做法的教堂，以及持续不断的鞭打威胁，这是一种挥之不去的心理负担。所有这一切都在剧本中得到了详细的记录，讲述了布朗在获得自由之前的故事，不仅包括他主人的冷酷对待，还讲述了比他自己更糟糕的条件。它是很重的材料，但它通过三个方式被减轻了。这个故事是叙述性的，而不是戏剧化的，如果没有魔术，故事就会显得平淡无奇。演员们的速度令人印象深刻，但表演却没有音调变化，让人很难跟上。故事的结局正如你所期望的那样开始：亨利·“博克斯”·布朗进入新生活。 • 在爱丁堡 Underbelly，直至 8 月 30 日 • 我们所有的爱丁堡音乐节评论
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
